card.title: How To Fix an iPad Pro 11in 4th Gen That Does Not Charge, CD3217 Solution

source.title: How To Fix an iPad Pro 11in 4th Gen That Does Not Charge, CD3217 Solution

claims.statement: iPad Pro 11 (4th gen) not charging, with a USB meter stuck at about 5 V / 0.62 A instead of negotiating 15 V, is normally a faulty CD3217 USB-C controller.
Check for shorts on the three large caps by CD3217: PP_LDO_CORE, PP3V3_ACE_LDO (usually the shorted one) and PP3V3_S2_ACE.
A replacement CD3217 must come from a donor board together with its paired ROM chip (U3890 on this model, usually marked 8Nxxxx); without the ROM the new chip will not work.

procedure: Rule out no-power with a charged battery or power supply.
Test with a known-good charge port.
Remove CD3217 and confirm shorts clear.
Fit donor CD3217 plus its paired ROM (U3890) from the same board.
Confirm 15 V charging on a USB meter.
